“Michelin Selected” authentic Vietnamese restaurant
May 2026 • Friends
Quán Ăn Ngon in Hanoi is a bustling, well-loved restaurant recognized by Michelin, serving a variety of authentic Vietnamese dishes that are both affordable and expertly prepared. 

Set in a charming colonial villa, it is especially renowned for bánh xèo—Vietnamese pancakes—and Bún chả, a Northern Hanoi specialty featuring charcoal-grilled pork served with a light, savory-sweet broth, cold rice vermicelli noodles, and fresh herbs. The menu also includes grilled dishes, fried rice, veggies, seafood, spring rolls, and regional specialties. Its vibrant, open-kitchen courtyard atmosphere makes it a favorite among locals and tourists alike. 

All the dishes we tried were fantastic, prepared with fresh ingredients and well-balanced flavors. We truly enjoyed the dining experience at this lively restaurant, which left a lasting memory.

Buzzy, busy and very tasty!
Mar 2025 • Couples
Last night in Vietnam. We had done a food tour in Hanoi which was fun and saw this restaurant which is set out a bit like the Time Out in Lisbon- a big central section of tables with food stations set around. Only here, they are not individual separate pop ups but stations that specialise in different sets of dishes (one soup, one vermicelli, one stir fry etc). We booked (a good plan as you may otherwise have to wait for a table) and had lots of smallish dishes between the four of us and a very nice bottle of Australian white for 950,000.

We enjoyed everything we ordered and agreed that this was the tastiest food we had eaten in Vietnam. Everything is served when it is ready so dishes come and go and the staff are efficient. We particularly enjoyed the mini shrimp pancakes (better than than the ordinary ones which were fattier), the pork ribs, the shrimp nem and the seafood vermicelli . Only one thing to be aware of: if it is cool outside, it can be cool inside as it is partially open and lets in the breeze! Thoroughly enjoyable! Cost for for just under 4M Dong.

The name of the restaurant, Quang Gong, seems to mean a delicious restaurant, with a variety of Vietnamese dishes! You can enjoy everything from street food to fine food! I guess it's fascinating that there are so many flavors from all over Vietnam.

In addition to the classic fresh spring rolls, banh mi, and stir-fried empty spinach salad, we had raw oysters and other dishes!
